figures.caption: Figure 2.4.2 shows the implementation of the front-end. The one-stage CTLE incorporates degeneration to create a maximum high-frequency boost of 8dB as well as inductive peaking to drive the DMUX with sufficient bandwidth. This stage also realizes offset cancellation by imbalancing the tail currents and without adding devices in the signal path. The DMUX employs passive switching but also boosts the sampled signal level by 6dB through the use of a regenerative charge-steering pair. With a 1dBcompression point of 180mVpp, this pair exhibits enough linearity for the odd and even DFEs to equalize the dispersed signal. Note that DMUX1 delivers NRZ outputs because the cross-coupled charge-steering latches merge the reset and sampling phases [1].

references.sentence: Shown in Fig. 2.4.1, the overall system consists of a continuous-time linear equalizer (CTLE), a 1-to-2 demultiplexer (DMUX1), and two half-rate/quarter-rate (HRQR) paths.
The architecture of Fig. 2.4.1 merits three remarks.
Figure 2.4.2 shows the implementation of the front-end.
Figure 2.4.3 presents the implementation of one half-rate/quarter-rate path (excluding tap 2 and RZ/NRZ conversion).
We note several attributes of the circuit in Fig. 2.4.3.
Third, the cross-coupled PMOS pair tied to X and Y in Fig. 2.4.3 prevents collapse of these nodes when both tap 1 and tap 2 branches draw charge.
Fifth, the multiplexing of the feedback components is accomplished through gating the tails in Fig. 2.4.3 by the 6.25GHz clock.
Figure 2.4.7 shows the die core, which measures 100×100μm2.
Figure 2.4.5 plots the BER as a function of the external clock phase, revealing an eye opening of approximately 0.44UI.
Figure 2.4.6 summarizes the measured performance of the equalizer and compares it with that of prior art.
